title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'Longue Marche' sequel 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Π = π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}: free profinite on two generators, written with loops ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ (product 1). L_i = ℓ_i^{Ẑ} are the inertia ('lacet') subgroups. Ĝ^+_{0,3} is an extension of 𝔖_3 by Π. In it σ_∞ is the involution exchanging 0 and 1, ρ is a lift of the 3-cycle, and ε_0 is an involution with ε_0^2 = ℓ_0.

The page fixes the class of objects to study: outer automorphisms of Π that respect the loop structure (they send each inertia class to a conjugate of a power) and commute with the outer 𝔖_3-action. Equivalently, these are outer automorphisms of Ĝ^+_{0,3} inducing the identity on 𝔖_3. The page normalises them to actual automorphisms u that fix σ_∞ and fix ρ modulo Π, so that ρuρ^{-1} = int(g)u (condition (38)).

The loop condition reads: there are p ∈ Ẑ* (the 'cyclotomic' exponent) and g_0 ∈ Π with u(ℓ_0) = int(g_0)(ℓ_0^p), formula (39). Here g_0 is determined modulo L_0, since the centraliser of ℓ_0 is L_0.

The claim is then (40): g = σ_∞(g_0)·ℓ_1^ν·ρ(g_0)^{-1}, with ν ∈ Ẑ uniquely determined and independent of the choice of g_0. Equivalently (41): σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g ρ(g_0) ∈ L_1, the centraliser of L_1.

The proof is on the next page:
- Apply u to σ_∞(L_0) = L_1.
- Use uσ_∞ = σ_∞u and u(L_1) = int(gρ(g_0))(L_1).
- Conclude that σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g ρ(g_0) normalises L_1.
- In a free profinite group an inertia subgroup is self-normalising, so this element lies in L_1.

The outcome is that such an automorphism is parametrised by (p, g_0 mod L_0, ν) subject to a relation. This is Grothendieck's own route to a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type parametrisation: a pair (λ, f) in Drinfeld's notation, with the extra 𝔖_3-symmetry. In effect he is deriving the 'two-cycle' and 'three-cycle' type relations from S_3-equivariance.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The derivation relies on the self-normalising property of inertia subgroups L_i in π̂_{0,3}, which holds for free profinite groups; it is stated without proof here and used on the next page.
Equation numbers (39)-(41) are reused: they clash with (39)-(41) on the previous page, so the numbering is being redone.
There is a notational clash between the exponent p ∈ Ẑ* and the 3-cycle ρ; the machine transcription confuses them.

ideas.what: Restricting to outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} that preserve inertia classes and commute with the S_3 outer action, recast as automorphisms of the extension Ĝ^+_{0,3} fixing σ_∞ and fixing ρ mod π̂_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT as an automorphism group of π̂_1(M_{0,4}) / of the tower; the S_3-equivariance (2- and 3-cycle relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; anticipated by Grothendieck's Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in outline; La Longue Marche (1981) for the Galois action on π̂_{0,3}

ideas.what: Parametrisation u(ℓ_0) = int(g_0)ℓ_0^p, g = σ_∞(g_0) ℓ_1^ν ρ(g_0)^{-1}, using self-normalisation of inertia subgroups
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of ĜT elements by (λ, f), with σ(x) = x^λ, σ(y) = f^{-1} y^λ f; self-normalising procyclic inertia subgroups in free profinite groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990; Ihara; Nakamura for the group-theoretic normaliser lemmas

missed.claim: This is Grothendieck's own unpublished derivation of GT-type relations from S_3-equivariance on π̂_{0,3}, with the extra parameter ν ∈ Ẑ. It predates or parallels Drinfeld's formulation. Mathematically the content is now standard; its interest is historical, documenting his independent approach.
missed.quote: g = σ_∞(g_0) ℓ_1^ν ρ(g_0)^{-1} avec ν ∈ Ẑ bien déterminé (indépendant du choix de g_0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical record of how Grothendieck approached ĜT through the 'loop equation' in the S_3-extension. The mathematics itself is covered by the later literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine step in what is now the theory of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Its only novelty is historical: it is Grothendieck's own formulation via Ĝ^+_{0,3}.
transcription_corrections: The exponent in (39) is p (in 'p ∈ Ẑ* et'), not ρ: it should read u(ℓ'_0) = int(g_0)(ℓ'_0^p), i.e. u(ℓ_0) = int(g_0)(ℓ_0^p).
'se pi... σ_∞' is likely 'i.e. qui fixent σ_∞'.
'ce cas [?] faits par ailleurs' is likely 'Des calculs faits par ailleurs montrent alors que...'.
In (41) the struck-out leading ρ(g_0) is deleted and ρ(g_0) is added after g. It reads σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g ρ(g_0) ∈ L_1 = Centr_{π̂_{0,3}}(L_1).
The marginal '(cl. ext.)' annotation may read '(effectivement)' or '(extérieurement)'; the image is ambiguous.
